name: Nuclear pairing is BCS pairing
summary: Odd-even mass staggering, the gap in even-even spectra and reduced moments of inertia follow from the BCS gap equation with a short-range NN attraction near the nuclear Fermi surface; Bohr, Mottelson and Pines carried BCS over to nuclei within a year.
breaks: Nuclei hold only ~10 pairs, so BCS particle-number fluctuations matter (projection needed) and the coherence length exceeds the nucleus; the pairing glue is the bare nuclear force, not a retarded phonon.
sources: Bohr, Mottelson & Pines (1958). "Possible Analogy between the Excitation Spectra of Nuclei and Those of the Superconducting Metallic State". *Phys. Rev.* 110, 936. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.110.936](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.110.936)

name: Rotation vs magnetic field: backbending and Meissner
summary: The Coriolis force on a rotating nucleus acts on time-reversed pairs as a magnetic field acts on Cooper pairs; pairing quenches the moment of inertia below the rigid value (like Meissner screening), and backbending at high spin is the analogue of the critical field that destroys superconductivity.
map: H'=H-\omega J_x\leftrightarrow H-\mu_B\mathbf B\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma;\ \mathcal I<\mathcal I_{\rm rigid}\leftrightarrow\chi<0;\ \omega_c\leftrightarrow H_c
breaks: The cranking 'field' couples to the orbital angular momentum of a finite drop, not to a gauge field; there is no flux expulsion, London length or vortex phase, and the transition is smeared by finite size.
sources: Mottelson & Valatin (1960). "Effect of Nuclear Rotation on the Pairing Correlation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 5, 511. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.5.511](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.5.511)

name: Pairing in finite Fermi systems: nuclei and nanograins
summary: Nuclei and nanometre Al grains are both mesoscopic superconductors whose level spacing is comparable to the gap; the exactly solvable Richardson pairing model describes both, and the nuclear odd-even mass effect is the parity effect seen in grain spectroscopy and superconducting single-electron transistors.
breaks: Grains have a Coulomb charging energy and an electron bath; nuclei have two particle species, deformation and spin-orbit-split shells, so level statistics and blocking differ.
sources: Richardson (1963). "A restricted class of exact eigenstates of the pairing-force Hamiltonian". *Phys. Lett.* 3, 277. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(63)90259-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(63)90259-2)

name: Neutron-star superfluids and superconducting protons
summary: The same gap equation predicts 1S0 neutron superfluidity in the crust, 3P2 neutron pairing and type-II proton superconductivity with flux tubes in the core; these set neutron-star cooling (pair-breaking neutrino emission), specific heat and rotational dynamics. Dilute neutron matter is close to the unitary Fermi gas.
breaks: Gaps are not measured directly and depend strongly on medium polarization and three-nucleon forces; the protons sit in a neutron superfluid with entrainment, a coupling absent in metals.
sources: Baym, Pethick & Pines (1969). "Superfluidity in Neutron Stars". *Nature* 224, 673. [doi:10.1038/224673a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/224673a0)

name: Pulsar glitches as vortex pinning and creep
summary: Glitches are explained by quantized neutron-superfluid vortices pinned to crust nuclei that unpin collectively, and post-glitch relaxation by thermally activated vortex creep: the Anderson-Kim flux-creep physics of type-II superconductors, carried to neutron stars by Anderson himself.
breaks: Neutron vortices are neutral (no flux, no Lorentz force); pinning energies and whether the crustal superfluid can store enough angular momentum (the entrainment problem) are disputed.
sources: Anderson & Itoh (1975). "Pulsar glitches and restlessness as a hard superfluidity phenomenon". *Nature* 256, 25. [doi:10.1038/256025a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/256025a0)

name: 3P2 neutron superfluid as triplet p-wave pairing
summary: Spin-triplet 3P2 neutron pairing in neutron-star cores has an anisotropic, multicomponent order parameter like superfluid 3He and the p-wave pairing behind topological superconductors, which raises the question of protected surface modes and half-quantum vortices in neutron stars.
breaks: The 3P2 channel is driven by the tensor and spin-orbit forces with L=1, S=1, J=2 rather than pure p-wave; the gap is uncertain by an order of magnitude and no observable topological signature has been identified.
sources: Dean & Hjorth-Jensen (2003). "Pairing in nuclear systems: from neutron stars to finite nuclei". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 607. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.75.607](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.75.607)

name: Band theory of dripped neutrons in the inner crust
summary: Free neutrons in the inner crust move in the periodic potential of the nuclear lattice, so Bloch band structure gives them an effective mass and entrainment by the crust; band calculations find most neutrons entrained, which feeds the glitch angular-momentum budget.
map: \psi_{n\mathbf k}(\mathbf r+\mathbf R)=e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf R}\psi_{n\mathbf k}(\mathbf r);\ n_n^{c}\propto\sum_{n\mathbf k}|\nabla_{\mathbf k}\epsilon_{n\mathbf k}|^2\delta(\epsilon-\mu)
breaks: Pairing, with a gap comparable to band splittings, smears band effects and is often neglected in band calculations; that is the main open question.
sources: Chamel (2012). "Neutron conduction in the inner crust of a neutron star in the framework of the band theory of solids". *Phys. Rev. C* 85, 035801. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevC.85.035801](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevC.85.035801)

name: Neutron-star crust as a bcc Coulomb crystal
summary: The outer crust is a body-centred-cubic lattice of neutron-rich nuclei in a degenerate relativistic electron gas; its composition follows from minimizing Madelung plus nuclear energies, and inner-crust calculations use the Wigner-Seitz cell method taken from solid-state physics.
breaks: The lattice 'atoms' are bare nuclei in a uniform relativistic electron gas (no chemical bonding), and the inner crust is penetrated by a neutron superfluid.
sources: Chamel & Haensel (2008). "Physics of Neutron Star Crusts". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 10. [arXiv:0812.3955](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3955)

name: Crust elasticity, phonons and magnetar oscillations
summary: The crust shear modulus and breaking strain come from the lattice dynamics of the Coulomb crystal (molecular dynamics gives a strain of ~0.1, far above terrestrial metals); crust torsional modes are candidates for magnetar-flare QPOs, and crust strength limits the mountains that would radiate gravitational waves.
breaks: Phonons of a Coulomb crystal in a compressible electron background have a plasma-frequency longitudinal branch, unlike the acoustic phonons of ordinary solids; superfluid neutrons add mixed modes.
sources: Horowitz & Kadau (2009). "Breaking Strain of Neutron Star Crust and Gravitational Waves". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 102, 191102. [arXiv:0904.1986](https://arxiv.org/abs/0904.1986)
Chamel & Haensel (2008). "Physics of Neutron Star Crusts". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 10. [arXiv:0812.3955](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3955)

name: Crust transport: conductivity, impurities and field decay
summary: Crust thermal and electrical conductivities are computed with metal transport theory (electron-phonon and electron-impurity scattering, Wiedemann-Franz); crust cooling after accretion outbursts shows a well-ordered, high-conductivity lattice, while a disordered pasta layer would be highly resistive.
breaks: The electrons are ultra-relativistic and fields reach 1e15 G, so magnetized quantum transport goes beyond terrestrial regimes.
sources: Brown & Cumming (2009). "Mapping Crustal Heating with the Cooling Light Curves of Quasi-Persistent Transients". *Astrophys. J.* 698, 1020. [arXiv:0901.3115](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.3115)

name: Nuclear pasta and block-copolymer microphase separation
summary: Pasta phases (spheres, rods, slabs, gyroid-like and inverted) come from competition between nuclear surface tension and long-range Coulomb energy; block-copolymer melts show the same morphology sequence because the Ohta-Kawasaki functional has the same short-range plus Coulomb-kernel structure.
breaks: Pasta is cold, quantum-degenerate matter with shell effects and electron screening; copolymer morphology is set by chain entropy and connectivity at finite temperature, and kinetics and defects differ.
sources: Ravenhall, Pethick & Wilson (1983). "Structure of Matter below Nuclear Saturation Density". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 50, 2066. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.2066](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.50.2066)

name: Nuclear pasta as liquid-crystal-like matter
summary: Rod and slab pasta phases have orientational and partial positional order like columnar and smectic liquid crystals, so their elasticity and topological defects (screw dislocations in slabs) are described with liquid-crystal elastic theory; this sets the pasta shear modulus and viscosity.
breaks: Pasta units are nuclear clusters ordered by Coulomb frustration, not anisotropic molecules; there is no molecular director and thermal fluctuations are weak.
sources: Caplan & Horowitz (2017). "Colloquium: Astromaterial science and nuclear pasta". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 89, 041002. [arXiv:1606.03646](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03646)

name: Planckian dissipation: QGP and strange metals
summary: The QGP's eta/s near hbar/(4 pi k_B) and the strange-metal scattering rate hbar/tau of order k_BT are both 'Planckian' transport set by hbar and T alone, and gauge/gravity duality has been applied to both as a model of strongly coupled matter without quasiparticles.
breaks: Strange-metal resistivity needs momentum relaxation by the lattice and disorder, while eta/s is a momentum-conserving diffusivity; the KSS value is not a proven bound, and holographic models are neither QCD nor cuprates.

name: Viscous electron flow and eta/s in metals vs QGP
summary: In ultraclean conductors electron-electron collisions dominate and charge flows hydrodynamically (Gurzhi effect, negative nonlocal resistance), giving measured electron viscosities that can be set against QGP eta/s in the same Navier-Stokes framework.
breaks: Fermi-liquid electrons are weakly coupled with a long l_ee, so their eta/s is far above the QGP value; momentum relaxation at boundaries and impurities has no QGP counterpart.

name: Chiral anomaly: CME in QGP and Weyl semimetals
summary: The axial anomaly that would drive a current along B in a chirally imbalanced QGP (the chiral magnetic effect) is the same anomaly equation behind the negative longitudinal magnetoresistance of Weyl and Dirac semimetals, where the effect is observed; in heavy-ion collisions the isobar run found no signal beyond background.
breaks: In the QGP the imbalance comes from gluon topological fluctuations and B lasts ~0.1 fm/c; in Weyl metals it is pumped by parallel E and B and relaxed by internode scattering, and lattice Weyl nodes come in pairs (Nielsen-Ninomiya).

name: Spin-vorticity: Lambda polarization and Barnett effect
summary: Global Lambda polarization in off-central collisions shows the QGP is the most vortical fluid known; it aligns spins through the same spin-rotation coupling as the Barnett effect and spin hydrodynamic generation in liquid metals.
breaks: QGP polarization is read from the hadronized final state of a ~10 fm/c fluid in local equilibrium; the spintronic versions involve electron spin, spin-orbit coupling and dissipative spin currents.

name: Colour superconductivity in dense quark matter
summary: At high baryon density the attractive colour-antitriplet channel makes the quark Fermi surface unstable to BCS pairing; the colour-flavour-locked phase is a colour superconductor in which gluons acquire Meissner masses and chiral symmetry breaks, a candidate for neutron-star cores.
breaks: The condensate breaks a non-abelian gauge symmetry and is under control only at asymptotic density; at neutron-star densities it is model-dependent and has no direct experimental confirmation.
sources: Alford, Rajagopal & Wilczek (1999). "Color-flavor locking and chiral symmetry breaking in high density QCD". *Nucl. Phys. B* 537, 443. [arXiv:hep-ph/9804403](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9804403)

name: Chiral condensate modelled on the BCS gap (NJL)
summary: Nambu and Jona-Lasinio built dynamical chiral symmetry breaking by direct analogy with BCS: the quark mass gap is a fermion-pair condensate, and its melting at the QCD crossover is the chiral-restoration signature studied in heavy-ion collisions.
breaks: The chiral condensate pairs particles with antiparticles and breaks a global, not a gauge, symmetry, so it gives Goldstone pions instead of a Meissner effect; the QCD transition is a crossover.

name: Nuclear energy density functionals as Kohn-Sham DFT
summary: Skyrme, Gogny and relativistic mean-field calculations are self-consistent Kohn-Sham-like schemes: nucleon orbitals in a potential that is the functional derivative of an energy density functional fitted to data, extended to pairing through HFB (compare DFT for superconductors).
map: h=\frac{\delta E[\rho,\tau,\mathbf J,\tilde\rho]}{\delta\rho},\ h\phi_i=\varepsilon_i\phi_i\ \leftrightarrow\ v_{\rm xc}=\frac{\delta E_{\rm xc}[n]}{\delta n}
breaks: Nuclei are self-bound with no external potential, so Hohenberg-Kohn applies only to intrinsic densities; nuclear EDFs break and then restore symmetries and are fitted phenomenologically rather than derived from a known exact functional.
sources: Bender, Heenen & Reinhard (2003). "Self-consistent mean-field models for nuclear structure". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 121. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.75.121](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.75.121)

name: Time-dependent DFT of fission and electron dynamics
summary: Microscopic fission dynamics (scission, fragment excitation, neutron emission) is computed with time-dependent superfluid DFT, the nuclear version of the Runge-Gross TDDFT used for electronic excitations and dynamics in materials.
breaks: Nuclear TDDFT lacks quantum fluctuations of the collective coordinates (no spontaneous tunnelling) and uses fitted functionals; electronic TDDFT has an external field and adiabatic xc approximations.

name: Homogeneous-matter QMC as functional input
summary: Electronic DFT rests on the QMC energy of the uniform electron gas (LDA); nuclear functionals are anchored the same way to ab initio neutron-matter equations of state, which fix the isovector part of Skyrme EDFs and their neutron-skin and radius predictions.
map: E_{xc}^{\rm LDA}=\int n\,\epsilon_{xc}^{\rm HEG}(n)\,d^3r\ \leftrightarrow\ E_{\rm EDF}\ \text{fitted to}\ E_{\rm PNM}(n)/N
breaks: The electron gas is Coulombic and the LDA is a controlled local limit; neutron matter has spin-isospin-dependent and three-body forces with theory uncertainties, and the map to finite nuclei is a fit, not an exact limit.

name: Shared quantum Monte Carlo toolkit and sign problem
summary: GFMC/AFDMC and nuclear lattice EFT (auxiliary-field Monte Carlo after a Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation) are the projector and determinant QMC used for Hubbard models; approximate SU(4) Wigner symmetry suppresses the nuclear sign problem as particle-hole symmetry does at half filling, and neural-network states now enter both.

name: SRG/IMSRG and Wegner flow equations
summary: The similarity renormalization group that softens nuclear forces and the in-medium SRG that decouples nuclear ground states are the continuous unitary flow equations introduced by Wegner and by Glazek and Wilson, which are also used for impurity and lattice models in condensed matter.
breaks: Nuclear SRG must track the induced three- and higher-body forces of a vacuum interaction; CM flows usually start from a fixed lattice Hamiltonian and track induced couplings differently.

name: Landau Fermi-liquid theory of nuclei and nuclear matter
summary: Independent-particle shells survive a strong NN force because the relevant objects are Landau quasiparticles near the Fermi surface; Migdal's theory of finite Fermi systems uses Landau parameters (effective mass, spin-isospin g') as electron Fermi-liquid theory does, and giant resonances are its zero-sound-like modes.
breaks: Nuclei are finite and self-bound with two species and a strong tensor force; quasiparticle lifetimes are short away from the Fermi surface and strength fragmentation is large.

name: Particle-vibration coupling vs electron-phonon coupling
summary: Bohr-Mottelson nuclear field theory couples single nucleons to quantized surface 'phonons' just as electrons couple to lattice phonons; the coupling dresses quasiparticles, fragments strength and adds an induced pairing interaction akin to phonon-mediated BCS glue.
map: H_{pv}=\sum_{\lambda\mu}\kappa_\lambda k(r)Y^*_{\lambda\mu}(\hat r)(b^\dagger_{\lambda\mu}+b_{\lambda\mu})\leftrightarrow\sum g_{\mathbf q}(b^\dagger_{\mathbf q}+b_{-\mathbf q})c^\dagger c

name: Shell structure and magic numbers in clusters and dots
summary: Alkali-metal clusters show magic numbers 8, 20, 40, 58 and quantum dots show shell filling with Hund's rule; both are understood with nuclear tools (mean-field shells, Strutinsky shell corrections, Nilsson-type deformation). Quantum dots are 'artificial atoms' and clusters 'electronic nuclei'.

breaks: Electron systems lack spin-orbit-driven magic numbers (no 28, 50, 82) and are Coulomb-repulsive and externally confined; nuclei are self-bound with short-range forces.

name: Giant dipole resonance and cluster surface plasmon
summary: The nuclear giant dipole resonance (protons oscillating against neutrons) and the Mie surface plasmon of metal clusters are both collective dipole modes that exhaust the Thomas-Reiche-Kuhn sum rule, treated with the same RPA and Goldhaber-Teller/Steinwedel-Jensen pictures.
breaks: The GDR restoring force is the isovector symmetry energy, the plasmon's is Coulomb; Landau damping and escape widths differ in size and origin.

name: Shape phase transitions as finite-size quantum criticality
summary: Along isotopic chains nuclei change from spherical to deformed as the control parameter N varies; Landau theory in quadrupole collective coordinates and the critical-point symmetries E(5)/X(5) treat this as a quantum phase transition with finite-N precursors.
breaks: Nuclei never reach a thermodynamic limit, N is discrete, and there is no spatial correlation length, quantum critical fan or non-Fermi-liquid transport.
sources: Cejnar, Jolie & Casten (2010). "Quantum phase transitions in the shapes of atomic nuclei". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 2155. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.82.2155](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.82.2155)

Iachello (2001). "Analytic Description of Critical-Point Nuclei in a Spherical-Axially Deformed Shape Phase Transition". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 87, 052502. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.052502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.052502)

name: Random-matrix statistics: compound nuclei and chaotic dots
summary: Random-matrix theory was born for neutron resonances (Wigner, Porter-Thomas), and its reaction-theory machinery (Mahaux-Weidenmüller S-matrix, Ericson fluctuations) became the theory of transport through chaotic quantum dots: conductance fluctuations and the Landauer conductance as S-matrix statistics.
map: S=1-2\pi iW^\dagger(E-H+i\pi WW^\dagger)^{-1}W,\ H\in\text{GOE};\ G=\frac{2e^2}{h}\mathrm{Tr}\,t^\dagger t
breaks: Nuclear widths probe energy-averaged cross sections of a self-bound system; dot transport adds magnetic-field symmetry classes (GUE), dephasing and Coulomb blockade.
sources: Porter & Thomas (1956). "Fluctuations of Nuclear Reaction Widths". *Phys. Rev.* 104, 483. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.104.483](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.104.483)
Mitchell, Richter & Weidenmüller (2010). "Random matrices and chaos in nuclear physics: Nuclear reactions". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 2845. [arXiv:1001.2422](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.2422)
Beenakker (1997). "Random-matrix theory of quantum transport". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 69, 731. [arXiv:cond-mat/9612179](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9612179)

name: Neutron scattering as the probe of structure and magnetism
summary: The nuclear neutron-scattering length (Fermi pseudopotential) and the neutron magnetic moment make reactor and spallation neutrons the standard probe of crystal structure, magnetic order and phonon and magnon dispersions; antiferromagnetic order was first seen this way.
breaks: b is an empirical nuclear quantity that varies erratically between isotopes (hence isotopic contrast variation), unlike X-ray form factors that scale with Z.
sources: Shull, Strauser & Wollan (1951). "Neutron Diffraction by Paramagnetic and Antiferromagnetic Substances". *Phys. Rev.* 83, 333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.83.333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.83.333)

name: Ion channeling, RBS and crystal-blocking lifetimes
summary: Nuclear backscattering and channeling of MeV ions locate impurities and defects in crystals; conversely, crystal blocking of reaction products measures compound-nucleus and fission lifetimes down to ~1e-18 s from the recoil distance travelled before decay.
breaks: Channeling is classical ion optics in a lattice; it gives timing only when recoil displacements are comparable with the Thomas-Fermi screening length.

name: Mössbauer effect: recoil-free gamma emission from a lattice
summary: Nuclear gamma rays are emitted and absorbed without recoil because the whole lattice takes the momentum; the recoil-free fraction is the phonon Debye-Waller factor, and Mössbauer spectroscopy reads hyperfine fields, isomer shifts and phonon densities of states in solids.
breaks: Only low-energy, long-lived gamma transitions (57Fe at 14.4 keV) work, and the nuclear linewidth, not phonon physics, sets the resolution.
sources: Mössbauer (1958). "Kernresonanzfluoreszenz von Gammastrahlung in Ir191". *Z. Phys.* 151, 124. [doi:10.1007/BF01344210](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01344210)

name: Thorium-229 nuclear clock in wide-gap crystals
summary: The 8.4 eV isomer of 229Th has been laser-excited in a CaF2 host: the crystal needs a band gap above the transition to suppress internal conversion, and crystal-field and electric-field-gradient effects split and shift the nuclear line.
breaks: The crystal is an environment, not part of the transition; defects, radiation damage and temperature-dependent shifts limit clock performance.
sources: Tiedau et al. (2024). "Laser Excitation of the Th-229 Nucleus". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 132, 182501. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.182501](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.182501)

name: Positron annihilation maps Fermi surfaces and vacancies
summary: Positrons from beta-plus sources (22Na) thermalize in solids and annihilate with electrons; the angular correlation and Doppler broadening of the 511 keV gammas map the electron momentum density (Fermi surfaces), and positron lifetimes identify vacancies.
map: \rho(\mathbf p)=\sum_j\left|\int e^{-i\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf r}\psi_+(\mathbf r)\psi_j(\mathbf r)\,d\mathbf r\right|^2;\ \Delta\theta\approx p_\perp/m_ec
breaks: The positron wavefunction and electron-positron correlations weight the signal non-uniformly, so momentum densities need theory corrections.
sources: Tuomisto & Makkonen (2013). "Defect identification in semiconductors with positron annihilation: Experiment and theory". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 85, 1583. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.85.1583](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.85.1583)

name: Cryogenic phonon calorimeters for double-beta and endpoints
summary: 0vbb searches (CUORE TeO2 crystals) and electron-capture endpoint measurements use millikelvin calorimeters in which the decay energy becomes phonons; the T^3 Debye heat capacity makes the temperature rise measurable with thermistors or transition-edge sensors.
breaks: Detector physics adds athermal phonon transport and superconducting-sensor physics beyond equilibrium lattice dynamics.
sources: CUORE Collaboration (2022). "Search for Majorana neutrinos exploiting millikelvin cryogenics with CUORE". *Nature* 604, 53. [arXiv:2104.06906](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.06906)

name: Semiconductor and scintillator radiation detectors
summary: HPGe and Si detectors are reverse-biased p-n junctions whose energy resolution is set by electron-hole pair statistics (about 3 eV per pair, Fano factor ~0.1); scintillators and halide-perovskite detectors depend on excitons, traps and band gaps.
breaks: Detector-grade operation needs ultrapure crystals with long carrier lifetimes and radiation hardness, priorities different from electronic devices.
sources: Fano (1947). "Ionization Yield of Radiations. II. The Fluctuations of the Number of Ions". *Phys. Rev.* 72, 26. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.72.26](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.72.26)
Kakavelakis et al. (2020). "Metal Halide Perovskites for High‐Energy Radiation Detection". *Adv. Sci.* 7, 2002098. [doi:10.1002/advs.202002098](https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202002098)

name: Neutron transmutation doping of silicon
summary: Irradiating float-zone silicon in a reactor turns 30Si into 31P by neutron capture and beta decay, giving the most uniform n-type doping available, used for high-power devices and thyristors.
breaks: Only n-type doping is possible, and the lattice damage has to be annealed.

name: Radiation damage in reactor materials
summary: Fast neutrons create displacement cascades in fuel cladding, steels and graphite; point-defect production, swelling, embrittlement and stored Wigner energy are solid-state physics that limits reactor lifetimes and fusion first walls.
breaks: Displacement counts overestimate surviving defects because of in-cascade recombination, so molecular dynamics is needed.
sources: Kinchin & Pease (1955). "The Displacement of Atoms in Solids by Radiation". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 18, 1. [doi:10.1088/0034-4885/18/1/301](https://doi.org/10.1088/0034-4885/18/1/301)

name: Collective tunnelling: fission and Josephson junctions
summary: Spontaneous fission and sub-barrier fusion are tunnelling of a collective coordinate coupled to many intrinsic degrees of freedom, the same dissipative macroscopic-tunnelling problem as the phase of a current-biased Josephson junction (Caldeira-Leggett).
breaks: The nuclear collective inertia M(q) and the barrier come from the same nucleons with level crossings, not an ohmic bath; the coupling is non-Markovian and few-channel.
sources: Caldeira & Leggett (1981). "Influence of Dissipation on Quantum Tunneling in Macroscopic Systems". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 46, 211. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.211](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.211)
Hagino & Takigawa (2012). "Subbarrier Fusion Reactions and Many-Particle Quantum Tunneling". *Prog. Theor. Phys.* 128, 1061. [arXiv:1210.1840](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.1840)

name: QGP epoch of the early universe
summary: The universe was a quark-gluon plasma until ~10 microseconds, when it cooled through the QCD crossover at T_c ~ 156 MeV; heavy-ion collisions recreate that matter, and the lattice equation of state measured there fixes the early-universe expansion rate through that epoch.
breaks: Heavy-ion fireballs have mu_B > 0 at lower energies, are tiny and expand in ~10 fm/c, and are not in global equilibrium; the cosmic transition is at mu_B ~ 0 and expands over microseconds.
sources: Aoki et al. (2006). "The order of the quantum chromodynamics transition predicted by the standard model of particle physics". *Nature* 443, 675. [arXiv:hep-lat/0611014](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/0611014)

name: Neutron-star mergers as nuclear laboratories
summary: Binary neutron-star mergers tie nuclear physics to multi-messenger signals: the EOS sets the inspiral tidal phase and remnant fate, and r-process nucleosynthesis powers the kilonova.
map: \tilde\Lambda\ \text{from GW phase}\ \leftrightarrow\ P(\varepsilon);\ L_{\rm KN}(t)\propto\dot\epsilon_{\rm r}(t)\approx t^{-1.3}
breaks: Mergers mix nuclear uncertainties with GR-MHD and neutrino transport uncertainties, so inferences are model-dependent.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2017). "GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 161101. [arXiv:1710.05832](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05832)
Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [doi:10.1038/nature24453](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature24453)

name: Nuclear burning powers stars and builds elements
summary: Thermonuclear reaction rates set the luminosity, lifetime and composition of stars at every stage, from pp burning through silicon burning and explosive nucleosynthesis.
sources: Bethe (1939). "Energy Production in Stars". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 434. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.434](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.434)
Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: Baryon density from BBN and CMB agree
summary: Deuterium from quasar absorbers gives Omega_b h^2 through BBN at ~1 percent, matching the CMB acoustic-peak value: two physically independent measurements of the same baryon-to-photon ratio, minutes and 380 kyr after the Big Bang.
breaks: The BBN value depends on nuclear rates (d(p,gamma)3He) and D/H systematics; the CMB value depends on the LambdaCDM fit.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)
Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: Dense-matter EOS sets neutron-star masses and radii
summary: The TOV equation turns the nuclear EOS into a mass-radius curve; 2-solar-mass pulsars, NICER radii and GW tidal deformabilities constrain matter up to several times saturation density.
sources: Demorest et al. (2010). "A two-solar-mass neutron star measured using Shapiro delay". *Nature* 467, 1081. [doi:10.1038/nature09466](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09466)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2018). "GW170817: Measurements of neutron star radii and equation of state". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 161101. [arXiv:1805.11581](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11581)

name: Supernovae as nucleosynthesis sites
summary: Core-collapse supernovae make the alpha elements and iron-peak nuclei through explosive burning and the nu-p and weak r-process; thermonuclear (Ia) supernovae make most of the iron. Ordinary core-collapse ejecta fail to reach the third r-process peak.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

Arnould, Goriely & Takahashi (2007). "The r-process of stellar nucleosynthesis: Astrophysics and nuclear physics achievements and mysteries". *Phys. Rep.* 450, 97. [arXiv:0705.4512](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4512)

name: Gamow-peak fusion sets stellar structure
summary: Stellar energy generation is set by sub-barrier fusion at the Gamow peak; the steep temperature dependence of the CNO cycle versus pp chain decides convective cores and the main-sequence mass-luminosity relation.
sources: Bethe (1939). "Energy Production in Stars". *Phys. Rev.* 55, 434. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.55.434](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.55.434)
Adelberger et al. (2011). "Solar fusion cross sections. II. The pp chain and CNO cycles". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 195. [arXiv:1004.2318](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2318)

name: Expansion rate versus weak freeze-out in BBN
summary: Primordial abundances are set where the Friedmann expansion rate overtakes the weak n-p conversion rate (T ~ 0.8 MeV) and the deuterium bottleneck opens (T ~ 0.07 MeV); BBN is therefore a test of cosmology at MeV temperatures, constraining N_eff and new physics.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Low-background radiation detectors for dark matter
summary: Dark-matter direct detection uses nuclear-physics detector technology (scintillators, HPGe, noble-liquid ionization) and radiation-protection-grade background control; nuclear-recoil quenching and gamma/neutron backgrounds are nuclear-physics problems.

name: Kilonova AT2017gfo and r-process nucleosynthesis
summary: The optical-infrared kilonova after GW170817 was powered by radioactive decay of freshly made r-process nuclei, and its red component showed lanthanide-rich ejecta, the first direct identification of an r-process site.
map: \kappa_{\rm lanth}\sim10\ \text{cm}^2\text{g}^{-1}\gg\kappa_{\rm Fe};\ t_{\rm peak}\approx\sqrt{\frac{\kappa M}{4\pi vc}}
sources: Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [doi:10.1038/nature24453](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature24453)
Pian et al. (2017). "Spectroscopic identification of r-process nucleosynthesis in a double neutron star merger". *Nature* 551, 67. [arXiv:1710.05858](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05858)

name: Stellar evolution drives s-process and burning stages
summary: Burning stages (H, He, C, Ne, O, Si) follow core contraction; thermal pulses in AGB stars release neutrons via 13C(alpha,n) and 22Ne(alpha,n) for the s-process, and the triple-alpha rate through the Hoyle state sets the C/O ratio.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: BBN plus BAO gives a CMB-independent H0
summary: Deuterium-calibrated BBN fixes the baryon density, which sets the sound horizon for BAO without CMB anisotropies; the resulting H0 agrees with Planck, so the Hubble tension is not a CMB-specific systematic. BBN also limits early-dark-energy and extra-radiation fixes through N_eff.
breaks: The result inherits LambdaCDM late-time assumptions and the d(p,gamma) rate uncertainty.
sources: Schöneberg, Lesgourgues & Hooper (2019). "The BAO+BBN take on the Hubble tension". *J. Cosmol. Astropart. Phys.* 10, 029. [arXiv:1907.11594](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.11594)
Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: BBN baryon budget demands non-baryonic dark matter
summary: BBN limits baryons to Omega_b ~ 0.05, while dynamics, lensing and the CMB need Omega_m ~ 0.3; most matter must therefore be non-baryonic, one of the strongest independent arguments for particle dark matter.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)
Planck Collaboration (2020). "Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters". *Astron. Astrophys.* 641, A6. [arXiv:1807.06209](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209)

name: BBN tests the Friedmann equation at MeV temperatures
summary: BBN abundances measure the radiation-dominated expansion rate H(T) and g_*, testing the Friedmann equation and the relativistic-species content 1-1000 s after the Big Bang, the earliest direct probe of the expansion history.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2016). "Big bang nucleosynthesis: Present status". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 88, 015004. [arXiv:1505.01076](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.01076)

name: Lithium problem: primordial or stellar depletion?
summary: Standard BBN predicts 7Li/H about three times the Spite plateau in metal-poor halo stars; whether the gap is nuclear (7Be destruction rates), stellar (atomic diffusion and mixing in stellar atmospheres) or new physics is unresolved, with stellar depletion now favoured.
sources: Fields (2011). "The Primordial Lithium Problem". *Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 61, 47. [arXiv:1203.3551](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.3551)

name: Lattice QCD equation of state and early-universe g_*
summary: The lattice QCD equation of state and susceptibilities, tested against heavy-ion data, give the effective degrees of freedom g_*(T) and g_*s(T) through the QCD crossover, which enter relic-abundance and axion-density calculations.
breaks: Cosmic use needs mu_B ~ 0 and full equilibrium, where lattice QCD is reliable; heavy-ion data mainly validate it.
sources: Borsanyi et al. (2016). "Calculation of the axion mass based on high-temperature lattice quantum chromodynamics". *Nature* 539, 69. [arXiv:1606.07494](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07494)

name: Tidal deformability from GW170817 constrains the EOS
summary: The GW170817 inspiral phase measured the binary tidal deformability, limiting neutron-star radii to ~11-13 km and excluding the stiffest nuclear EOS; joint analyses with NICER and nuclear data now bound pressure at twice saturation density.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2018). "GW170817: Measurements of neutron star radii and equation of state". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 161101. [arXiv:1805.11581](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11581)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2017). "GW170817: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Neutron Star Inspiral". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 161101. [arXiv:1710.05832](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05832)

name: EOS in core collapse and proto-neutron stars
summary: Core bounce, proto-neutron-star contraction, neutrino-driven explosion and black-hole formation depend on the finite-temperature nuclear EOS (stiffness, symmetry energy, nuclear statistical equilibrium composition).
breaks: Supernova EOS tables need finite temperature and proton fraction 0.05-0.5, beyond the cold beta-equilibrium EOS of neutron stars.
sources: Janka et al. (2007). "Theory of core-collapse supernovae". *Phys. Rep.* 442, 38. [arXiv:astro-ph/0612072](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0612072)

name: Maximum mass from merger remnants and short GRBs
summary: Whether a merger remnant collapses promptly, after a delay, or survives as a magnetar depends on the maximum neutron-star mass; the GW170817 short GRB and kilonova energetics argued for delayed collapse, suggesting M_max of about 2.2-2.3 solar masses.
map: M_{\rm thr}\approx kM_{\rm max},\ k\sim1.3\text{–}1.7;\ M_{\rm TOV}\lesssim2.2\text{–}2.3\,M_\odot
breaks: The argument depends on interpreting the kilonova ejecta and jet energetics, which are model-dependent.
sources: Margalit & Metzger (2017). "Constraining the Maximum Mass of Neutron Stars from Multi-messenger Observations of GW170817". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 850, L19. [arXiv:1710.05938](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05938)

name: Magnetar crusts: starquakes, QPOs and outbursts
summary: Magnetar bursts, giant flares and possibly FRBs are driven by crust stresses from evolving 1e15 G fields; crust breaking strain, shear modulus and seismic modes from nuclear and crust physics set burst energetics and QPO frequencies.
map: E_{\rm el}\sim\mu\,\epsilon_{\rm br}^2V_{\rm crust}/2;\ f_{\rm torsional}\approx\frac{v_t}{2\pi R}\sqrt{\ell(\ell+1)}\sim20\text{–}100\ \text{Hz}
breaks: Whether FRBs come from crust events or from magnetospheric or wind processes is unresolved.
sources: Kaspi & Beloborodov (2017). "Magnetars". *Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.* 55, 261. [arXiv:1703.00068](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.00068)

name: Neutron stars as dark-matter detectors
summary: Dark matter captured by scattering on neutron-star nucleons would heat old neutron stars; the capture rate uses the same dark-matter-nucleon cross section as direct detection, with neutron-star nuclear matter and Pauli blocking replacing the target nucleus.
breaks: Capture in dense matter involves strong-interaction medium effects and relativistic kinematics, and no candidate star has been observed at the required temperature.
sources: Baryakhtar et al. (2017). "Dark Kinetic Heating of Neutron Stars and An Infrared Window On WIMPs, SIMPs, and Pure Higgsinos". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 131801. [arXiv:1704.01577](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.01577)

name: Collapsars as r-process sites
summary: Neutron-rich accretion-disk outflows in collapsars (the engines of long GRBs) may make r-process material comparable to mergers, which would explain early-galaxy enrichment; near-infrared follow-up of long GRBs is testing this.
breaks: Disk-outflow Y_e depends on neutrino transport and magnetic physics that simulations do not yet agree on.
sources: Siegel, Barnes & Metzger (2019). "Collapsars as a major source of r-process elements". *Nature* 569, 241. [arXiv:1810.00098](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.00098)

name: Magnetar giant flares as r-process sites
summary: Delayed MeV gamma-ray emission after the 2004 SGR 1806-20 giant flare matches radioactive decay of freshly synthesized r-process nuclei in baryon-loaded ejecta, suggesting magnetars contribute a few percent of the r-process.
breaks: Single-event evidence; the ejecta mass and Y_e are inferred from models.
sources: Patel et al. (2025). "Direct Evidence for r-process Nucleosynthesis in Delayed MeV Emission from the SGR 1806–20 Magnetar Giant Flare". *Astrophys. J. Lett.*. [arXiv:2501.09181](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09181)

name: Galactic archaeology of r-process-enhanced stars
summary: Europium-rich metal-poor halo stars, the actinide-boost class and the single-event enrichment of the dwarf galaxy Reticulum II test which sites (rare, prolific mergers or collapsars) made the Milky Way's r-process elements and when.
breaks: Merger delay times and natal kicks complicate the link between abundance trends and sites.
sources: Ji et al. (2016). "R-process enrichment from a single event in an ancient dwarf galaxy". *Nature* 531, 610. [arXiv:1512.01558](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01558)

Arnould, Goriely & Takahashi (2007). "The r-process of stellar nucleosynthesis: Astrophysics and nuclear physics achievements and mysteries". *Phys. Rep.* 450, 97. [arXiv:0705.4512](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.4512)

name: Nucleosynthesis yields drive galactic chemical evolution
summary: Galaxy-formation simulations and chemical-evolution models use stellar and explosive yields (alpha elements from core collapse, Fe from Ia, s from AGB, r from mergers) as inputs; alpha/Fe ratios then clock star-formation histories.
sources: Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler & Hoyle (1957). "Synthesis of the Elements in Stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 29, 547. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.29.547)

name: s-process in AGB stars and barium/CEMP binaries
summary: Barium stars and carbon-enhanced metal-poor (CEMP-s) stars got their s-process overabundances by mass transfer from an AGB companion, so binary populations map the s-process yields and neutron exposures of extinct AGB stars.
sources: Escorza et al. (2026). "Stellar nucleosynthesis in the era of large surveys: S-process polluted binaries in GALAH DR4". *arXiv preprint*. [arXiv:2604.15197](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15197)

name: Radioactive 56Ni-56Co decay powers supernova light curves
summary: Type Ia and stripped-envelope supernova light curves are powered by 56Ni -> 56Co -> 56Fe decay (6.1 d and 77 d), so the peak luminosity measures the nickel mass (Arnett's rule) and the tail follows the cobalt half-life; 44Ti maps in Cas A trace explosion asymmetry.
map: ^{56}\mathrm{Ni}\xrightarrow{6.1\,\rm d}{}^{56}\mathrm{Co}\xrightarrow{77\,\rm d}{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe};\ L_{\rm peak}\approx\dot E_{\rm Ni}(t_{\rm peak});\ L_{\rm tail}\propto e^{-t/111\,\rm d}
breaks: Gamma-ray escape and positron trapping make the deposited luminosity differ from the decay luminosity at late times.
sources: Grefenstette et al. (2014). "Asymmetries in core-collapse supernovae from maps of radioactive 44Ti in CassiopeiaA". *Nature* 506, 339. [arXiv:1403.4978](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.4978)

name: Radioactive heating of kilonova ejecta
summary: Kilonovae are powered by the summed beta decays and fission of thousands of r-process nuclei, giving a heating rate close to t^-1.3; the luminosity therefore measures ejected r-process mass.
breaks: Thermalization efficiency and the uncertain beta-decay rates and masses of neutron-rich nuclei limit the mass inference to a factor of a few.
sources: Metzger et al. (2010). "Electromagnetic Counterparts of Compact Object Mergers Powered by the Radioactive Decay of R-process Nuclei". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 406, 2650. [arXiv:1001.5029](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.5029)
Kasen et al. (2017). "Origin of the heavy elements in binary neutron-star mergers from a gravitational-wave event". *Nature* 551, 80. [doi:10.1038/nature24453](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature24453)

name: 26Al heating and chronometry of the early Solar System
summary: Excess 26Mg in meteoritic inclusions shows live 26Al (t1/2 = 0.72 Myr) was present when the first solids formed; its decay heat melted and differentiated planetesimals, and short-lived radionuclides give Myr-resolution chronologies of disk evolution.
breaks: Dating assumes 26Al was homogeneously distributed in the disk, which is debated.
sources: Lee, Papanastassiou & Wasserburg (1976). "Demonstration of 26Mg excess in Allende and evidence for 26Al". *Geophys. Res. Lett.* 3, 41. [doi:10.1029/GL003i001p00041](https://doi.org/10.1029/GL003i001p00041)

name: Electron capture and weak rates in core collapse
summary: Electron captures on iron-group and neutron-rich nuclei (Gamow-Teller strength from the shell model) deleptonize the collapsing core and set the homologous-core mass, shock energy and neutrino signal of core-collapse supernovae.
breaks: Gamow-Teller strength of hot, neutron-rich nuclei far from stability is only partly measured; tables extrapolate shell-model and QRPA results.
sources: Langanke & Martínez-Pinedo (2003). "Nuclear weak-interaction processes in stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 819. [arXiv:nucl-th/0203071](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0203071)

name: Urca processes and neutrino cooling of compact stars
summary: Neutron stars cool by direct and modified Urca beta processes whose rates depend on the proton fraction and pairing; accreting crusts hold Urca shells, and electron capture onto nuclei sets white-dwarf and crust compositions.
map: n\to pe\bar\nu_e,\ pe\to n\nu_e;\ \text{direct Urca if }x_p\gtrsim0.11;\ \epsilon_{\rm dU}\propto T^6,\ \epsilon_{\rm mU}\propto T^8
breaks: The proton fraction and pairing gaps in the core are uncertain, so cooling curves constrain them only jointly.
sources: Langanke & Martínez-Pinedo (2003). "Nuclear weak-interaction processes in stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 819. [arXiv:nucl-th/0203071](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0203071)
Dean & Hjorth-Jensen (2003). "Pairing in nuclear systems: from neutron stars to finite nuclei". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 607. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.75.607](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.75.607)

name: Solar neutrinos measure pp-chain and CNO burning
summary: Neutrino fluxes from the pp chain (pp, 7Be, 8B) and the first detection of CNO neutrinos test laboratory fusion cross sections in the solar core; the CNO flux bears on the solar metallicity (abundance) problem raised by helioseismology.
breaks: Interpreting fluxes needs neutrino oscillation (MSW) parameters and the solar model's opacities.
sources: Adelberger et al. (2011). "Solar fusion cross sections. II. The pp chain and CNO cycles". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 195. [arXiv:1004.2318](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2318)
Borexino Collaboration (2020). "Experimental evidence of neutrinos produced in the CNO fusion cycle in the Sun". *Nature* 587, 577. [arXiv:2006.15115](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15115)

name: Carbon fusion rate and thermonuclear ignition
summary: Carbon ignition in white dwarfs (Type Ia supernovae), carbon flashes and X-ray superbursts depend on the low-energy 12C+12C fusion rate, whose resonant structure below 2 MeV remains uncertain.
breaks: Laboratory data stop above the Gamow window, and electron screening in dense plasmas modifies the rate.
sources: Tan et al. (2024). "Coincident measurement of the C12+C12 fusion cross section via the differential thick-target technique". *Phys. Rev. C* 110, 035808. [doi:10.1103/physrevc.110.035808](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevc.110.035808)

name: Deuterium burning separates brown dwarfs from planets
summary: The deuterium-burning mass limit (~13 Jupiter masses) is the conventional boundary between giant planets and brown dwarfs; it is set by when the core reaches the D(p,gamma)3He Gamow window before electron degeneracy halts contraction.
breaks: The limit depends on helium and deuterium fraction and metallicity; formation mode, not burning, may be the better planet criterion.
sources: Spiegel, Burrows & Milsom (2011). "The Deuterium-burning Mass Limit for Brown Dwarfs and Giant Planets". *Astrophys. J.* 727, 57. [arXiv:1008.5150](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.5150)

name: Nuclear structure factors for WIMP-nucleus scattering
summary: Spin-independent and spin-dependent dark-matter rates need nuclear form factors and structure functions computed with the shell model and chiral-EFT currents; the nonrelativistic EFT of direct detection maps each operator onto distinct nuclear responses.
breaks: Two-body currents and nuclear-structure uncertainties grow at large momentum transfer and for odd-unpaired nuclei.
sources: Fitzpatrick et al. (2013). "The Effective Field Theory of Dark Matter Direct Detection". *J. Cosmol. Astropart. Phys.* 02, 004. [arXiv:1203.3542](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.3542)

Klos et al. (2013). "Large-scale nuclear structure calculations for spin-dependent WIMP scattering with chiral effective field theory currents". *Phys. Rev. D* 88, 083516. [arXiv:1304.7684](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.7684)

name: Coherent neutrino-nucleus scattering and the neutrino fog
summary: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering, observed by COHERENT, gives nuclear recoils indistinguishable from WIMP signals; solar 8B and atmospheric neutrinos thus form the neutrino fog of direct detection, with rates set by the weak charge and neutron form factor.
breaks: The neutrino background is irreducible only for the same recoil spectrum; directionality and target complementarity partly separate it.
sources: COHERENT Collaboration (2017). "Observation of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering". *Science* 357, 1123. [arXiv:1708.01294](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.01294)

name: Cosmic-ray spallation and Li-Be-B production
summary: Spallation of cosmic-ray C, N, O on interstellar H and He makes Li, Be and B; secondary-to-primary ratios such as B/C measure the grammage traversed and calibrate Galactic propagation, so they rest on nuclear fragmentation cross sections.
breaks: Fragmentation cross sections are known to only 10-20 percent, which now limits AMS-02 propagation analyses.

name: Giant-dipole photodisintegration of UHE cosmic-ray nuclei
summary: Ultra-high-energy nuclei are destroyed by photodisintegration when CMB and infrared photons, boosted into the nucleus frame, hit the giant dipole resonance; this shapes the composition and cutoff of the UHECR spectrum alongside the GZK pion threshold for protons.
breaks: Photonuclear cross sections for unstable intermediate nuclei are model-based, and source composition is degenerate with propagation.
sources: Puget, Stecker & Bredekamp (1976). "Photonuclear interactions of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays and their astrophysical consequences". *Astrophys. J.* 205, 638. [doi:10.1086/154321](https://doi.org/10.1086/154321)

name: QGP-like collectivity and the air-shower muon puzzle
summary: Air showers contain more muons than hadronic models predict; strangeness enhancement and core-corona collectivity seen in high-multiplicity LHC collisions, implemented in models such as EPOS, are candidate explanations, linking QGP signatures to cosmic-ray composition.
breaks: Air showers involve forward-rapidity, light-ion collisions beyond collider coverage, so the extrapolation is uncertain.
sources: Pierog et al. (2015). "EPOS LHC: Test of collective hadronization with data measured at the CERN Large Hadron Collider". *Phys. Rev. C* 92, 034906. [arXiv:1306.0121](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0121)
ALICE Collaboration (2017). "Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity proton–proton collisions". *Nature Phys.* 13, 535. [arXiv:1606.07424](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07424)

name: Antinuclei: coalescence and absorption for dark matter
summary: Antideuterons and antihelium in cosmic rays would be a near background-free dark-matter signature; coalescence parameters measured in heavy-ion and pp collisions and ALICE's antihelium absorption cross sections set both the expected signal and the cosmic-ray background.
breaks: Coalescence depends on source size, which differs between Galactic dark-matter annihilation and collider systems.
sources: ALICE Collaboration (2023). "Measurement of anti-3He nuclei absorption in matter and impact on their propagation in the Galaxy". *Nature Phys.* 19, 61. [arXiv:2202.01549](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.01549)

name: PDFs set ultra-high-energy neutrino cross sections
summary: The neutrino-nucleon cross section above ~10 TeV is deep-inelastic scattering dominated by small-x sea quarks and gluons; IceCube's Earth-absorption measurement agrees with PDF-based predictions, and small-x uncertainty (and saturation) sets the high-energy event rate.
breaks: At the highest energies the relevant x lies below HERA's reach, so predictions extrapolate DGLAP or invoke saturation.
sources: IceCube Collaboration (2017). "Measurement of the multi-TeV neutrino interaction cross-section with IceCube using Earth absorption". *Nature* 551, 596. [arXiv:1711.08119](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.08119)

name: Fission yields shape r-process patterns and kilonovae
summary: Fission of the heaviest r-process nuclei recycles material to the second peak, shapes the rare-earth abundances and, through 254Cf, can dominate late-time kilonova heating; fission barriers and yields far from stability are a major r-process uncertainty.
breaks: Barriers and fragment yields of neutron-rich actinides come from models without measurements.
sources: Zhu et al. (2018). "Californium-254 and Kilonova Light Curves". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 863, L23. [arXiv:1806.09724](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.09724)

name: Quark-matter cores in massive neutron stars
summary: Model-agnostic EOS inference combining perturbative QCD at high density with nuclear EFT at low density finds the speed of sound and polytropic index in the cores of ~2-solar-mass stars consistent with deconfined quark matter.
breaks: The criterion is a heuristic; hadronic matter with a peaked sound speed can mimic it, so the claim is contested.
sources: Annala et al. (2020). "Evidence for quark-matter cores in massive neutron stars". *Nature Phys.* 16, 907. [arXiv:1903.09121](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.09121)

name: Nuclear masses fix the outer-crust composition
summary: The outer-crust sequence of nuclei (56Fe, 62Ni, ..., 78Ni, 82Zn and beyond toward the drip line) follows from measured and extrapolated masses of neutron-rich nuclei; Penning-trap mass measurements at radioactive-beam facilities move the predicted layers.
breaks: The deeper outer crust needs masses beyond experimental reach, so model mass tables take over.
sources: Chamel & Haensel (2008). "Physics of Neutron Star Crusts". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 10. [arXiv:0812.3955](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3955)

name: Evaluated reaction-rate libraries for stellar models
summary: Stellar evolution and explosion codes use evaluated thermonuclear rate compilations (REACLIB, NACRE) built from nuclear data and Hauser-Feshbach theory, so evaluation and covariance methods from nuclear data propagate into stellar predictions.
breaks: Many network rates are theoretical; uncertainties are correlated and often lack covariance information.
sources: Cyburt et al. (2010). "The JINA REACLIB Database: Its Recent Updates and Impact on Type-I X-ray Bursts". *Astrophys. J. Suppl.* 189, 240. [doi:10.1088/0067-0049/189/1/240](https://doi.org/10.1088/0067-0049/189/1/240)

name: Nuclear radiation detectors as gamma-ray telescopes
summary: MeV gamma-ray astronomy (nuclear lines, GRBs) uses nuclear-spectroscopy detectors: NaI and BGO scintillators, HPGe spectrometers (INTEGRAL/SPI) and Compton telescopes, with the same photoelectric/Compton/pair physics and activation backgrounds.
breaks: Space instruments face cosmic-ray activation and must reject a large instrumental background.

name: QGP as a colour plasma
summary: Above T_c the QGP screens colour charge and supports collective plasma oscillations like an electromagnetic plasma, with a Debye mass m_D ~ gT and plasma frequency ~ gT/3; this plasma language organizes its thermodynamics and transport.
breaks: Gluons carry colour and self-interact (non-abelian), the coupling near T_c is strong rather than weak, magnetic screening is non-perturbative, and the plasma confines into hadrons below T_c.
sources: Blaizot & Iancu (2002). "The quark-gluon plasma: collective dynamics and hard thermal loops". *Phys. Rep.* 359, 355. [arXiv:hep-ph/0101103](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0101103)

name: D-T fusion as the energy source of magnetic confinement
summary: Magnetic confinement fusion exists to run nuclear fusion reactions; the D-T cross section, its 3.5 MeV alpha and 14.1 MeV neutron set plasma heating, wall loading and the fuel cycle of tokamaks and stellarators.
map: \mathrm D+\mathrm T\to\alpha(3.5\,\text{MeV})+n(14.1\,\text{MeV});\ P_{\rm fus}=n_Dn_T\langle\sigma v\rangle E_{\rm fus}
sources: Bosch & Hale (1992). "Improved formulas for fusion cross-sections and thermal reactivities". *Nucl. Fusion* 32, 611. [doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07)

name: D-T reactivity sets the tokamak operating point
summary: The D-T reactivity peaks near 60-70 keV, but the triple product n T tau_E is minimized near 14 keV, which sets the ion temperature tokamaks aim for and the confinement time they must reach at the beta limit.
map: n\tau_E>\frac{12k_BT}{\langle\sigma v\rangle E_\alpha};\ nT\tau_E\gtrsim3\times10^{21}\ \text{keV s m}^{-3}\ \text{at}\ T\approx14\ \text{keV}
sources: Bosch & Hale (1992). "Improved formulas for fusion cross-sections and thermal reactivities". *Nucl. Fusion* 32, 611. [doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07)
Lawson (1957). "Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor". *Proc. Phys. Soc. B* 70, 6. [doi:10.1088/0370-1301/70/1/303](https://doi.org/10.1088/0370-1301/70/1/303)

name: Fuel cycles: D-T versus D-D, D-3He and p-11B
summary: Choice of fusion fuel trades reactivity against neutron production: D-T ignites at the lowest temperature but makes 80 percent of its energy as neutrons, while D-3He and p-11B are nearly aneutronic but need ~5-10 times higher temperatures where bremsstrahlung losses compete.
map: P_{\rm br}\propto Z_{\rm eff}n_e^2T^{1/2}\ \text{vs}\ P_{\rm fus}\propto n^2\langle\sigma v\rangle;\ \langle\sigma v\rangle_{\rm DT}/\langle\sigma v\rangle_{\rm DD}\sim100
sources: Bosch & Hale (1992). "Improved formulas for fusion cross-sections and thermal reactivities". *Nucl. Fusion* 32, 611. [doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07)

name: Fusion and fission share neutronics, blankets and materials
summary: Burning-plasma devices inherit fission-reactor neutron transport, shielding, activation and materials-damage methods and data; fusion's 14 MeV neutrons cause higher displacement and transmutation (helium) damage per neutron than fission spectra.

name: Fusion yield, alpha heating and ignition in ICF
summary: Inertial fusion needs a hot-spot areal density large enough to stop the 3.5 MeV alphas so that self-heating outruns losses; NIF's 2022 shot exceeded unity target gain. The D-T reactivity and alpha stopping power set the ignition condition.
map: \rho R_{\rm hs}\gtrsim0.3\ \text{g cm}^{-2},\ T_{\rm hs}\gtrsim5\ \text{keV};\ f_{\rm burn}\approx\frac{\rho R}{\rho R+6\ \text{g cm}^{-2}}
breaks: ICF yields are also limited by hydrodynamic instabilities and mix, which are not nuclear physics.
sources: Abu-Shawareb et al. (2024). "Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 132, 065102. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.065102](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.065102)
Bosch & Hale (1992). "Improved formulas for fusion cross-sections and thermal reactivities". *Nucl. Fusion* 32, 611. [doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07)

name: Alpha self-heating and the Lawson criterion
summary: A burning plasma is one in which fusion alphas supply most of the heating; the Lawson/ignition criterion follows from balancing alpha power (from the D-T reactivity) against transport and radiation losses, and alpha populations drive Alfvén eigenmodes.
map: \tfrac14n^2\langle\sigma v\rangle E_\alpha\geq\frac{3nk_BT}{\tau_E}+P_{\rm rad};\ Q=\frac{P_{\rm fus}}{P_{\rm heat}}\to\infty\ \text{(ignition)}
sources: Lawson (1957). "Some Criteria for a Power Producing Thermonuclear Reactor". *Proc. Phys. Soc. B* 70, 6. [doi:10.1088/0370-1301/70/1/303](https://doi.org/10.1088/0370-1301/70/1/303)
Bosch & Hale (1992). "Improved formulas for fusion cross-sections and thermal reactivities". *Nucl. Fusion* 32, 611. [doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07)

name: Spin-polarized fusion fuel
summary: Aligning D and T nuclear spins raises the D-T cross section by up to 50 percent because the reaction proceeds through the 3/2+ 5He resonance; whether polarization survives plasma depolarization processes is the open question.
breaks: Wall recycling, collisions and magnetic-field inhomogeneity can depolarize fuel; no reactor-scale test exists.
sources: Kulsrud et al. (1982). "Fusion Reactor Plasmas with Polarized Nuclei". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 1248. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1248](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1248)

name: Electron screening of fusion rates in plasmas
summary: Debye screening of the Coulomb barrier by plasma electrons and ions raises stellar fusion rates (Salpeter weak-screening factor); laboratory screening enhancements at low energy exceed the adiabatic prediction, a long-standing puzzle.
breaks: The weak-screening formula fails at strong coupling and in dynamic regimes; lab screening potentials U_e exceed theory by roughly a factor of two.
sources: Salpeter (1954). "Electron Screening and Thermonuclear Reactions". *Aust. J. Phys.* 7, 373. [doi:10.1071/PH540373](https://doi.org/10.1071/PH540373)

name: Pycnonuclear fusion in strongly coupled plasmas
summary: In white-dwarf interiors and accreted neutron-star crusts (Gamma >> 1) fusion proceeds by zero-point tunnelling between neighbouring lattice ions; the enhancement factors are computed with one-component-plasma Monte Carlo free energies.
breaks: Pycnonuclear rates are uncertain by orders of magnitude because of lattice dynamics, impurities and quantum effects.
sources: Ichimaru (1993). "Nuclear fusion in dense plasmas". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 65, 255. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.65.255](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.65.255)

name: Neutron-star crust as a one-component plasma
summary: The crust ions in a degenerate electron sea are a classical one-component (Yukawa-screened) plasma; it crystallizes at Gamma ~ 175, the same phase diagram in (Gamma, kappa) as dusty-plasma crystals and ultracold neutral plasmas.
breaks: Crust ions sit in a relativistic degenerate electron gas at 1e6-1e14 g/cc and may be quantum (ion plasma temperature) at the deepest layers; dusty plasmas are dissipative and charge-fluctuating.
sources: Chamel & Haensel (2008). "Physics of Neutron Star Crusts". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 10. [arXiv:0812.3955](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3955)

name: Strongly coupled QGP and strongly coupled plasmas
summary: RHIC's 'perfect liquid' was interpreted as a strongly coupled plasma with Coulomb-like coupling Gamma of order 1-3, borrowing classical strongly coupled plasma phenomenology (liquid-like correlations, low viscosity at intermediate Gamma).
breaks: QGP coupling is quantum and relativistic with colour degrees of freedom; Gamma is not a sharp control parameter, and QGP minimal viscosity has a quantum origin (eta/s ~ hbar/4pi).
sources: Shuryak (2005). "What RHIC experiments and theory tell us about properties of quark-gluon plasma?". *Nucl. Phys. A* 750, 64. [arXiv:hep-ph/0405066](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0405066)

name: Hard thermal loops: non-abelian Vlasov and Landau damping
summary: Hard-thermal-loop effective theory of the QGP is equivalent to colour Vlasov equations for hard particles in soft gauge fields; it gives Debye screening, Landau damping of gluon modes and plasmon dispersion exactly parallel to Vlasov-Maxwell plasma theory.
map: v\cdot\partial_x\,\delta n^a+g\,\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf E^a\frac{dn_0}{dp}=0\ \leftrightarrow\ \partial_tf+\mathbf v\cdot\nabla f+\frac{q}{m}\mathbf E\cdot\nabla_vf=0
breaks: Gauge covariance requires adjoint colour transport and non-abelian field strengths; the theory holds only at weak coupling g << 1, far from RHIC/LHC conditions.
sources: Blaizot & Iancu (2002). "The quark-gluon plasma: collective dynamics and hard thermal loops". *Phys. Rep.* 359, 355. [arXiv:hep-ph/0101103](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0101103)

name: Colour Debye screening melts quarkonia
summary: Debye screening of the heavy-quark potential in the QGP dissolves J/psi and Upsilon states once the screening length falls below their radius, giving sequential suppression ordered by binding energy.
breaks: Quarkonia also acquire imaginary potential (Landau damping width) and regenerate by recombination at the LHC, so suppression is not pure static screening.
sources: Matsui & Satz (1986). "J/ψ suppression by quark-gluon plasma formation". *Phys. Lett. B* 178, 416. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(86)91404-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(86)91404-8)

name: Weibel-type plasma instabilities in QGP thermalization
summary: Momentum-space anisotropy of the early glasma drives chromo-Weibel instabilities, the non-abelian counterpart of filamentation in anisotropic electromagnetic plasmas, which accelerate isotropization in bottom-up thermalization.
breaks: Non-abelian self-interaction saturates growth differently than in QED plasmas, and the role of instabilities versus scattering in thermalization is debated.
sources: Arnold, Lenaghan & Moore (2003). "QCD plasma instabilities and bottom-up thermalization". *J. High Energy Phys.* 08, 002. [arXiv:hep-ph/0307325](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0307325)

name: Parton energy loss and heavy-quark diffusion as kinetics
summary: Collisional energy loss of fast partons and heavy-quark diffusion are treated with Fokker-Planck and Langevin equations for a test particle in a plasma, as for fast ions slowing in fusion plasmas; q-hat is the transverse momentum diffusion coefficient.
breaks: Radiative (BDMPS) loss dominates for light partons and has coherence effects with no classical-plasma analogue.
sources: Moore & Teaney (2005). "How much do heavy quarks thermalize in a heavy ion collision?". *Phys. Rev. C* 71, 064904. [arXiv:hep-ph/0412346](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0412346)

name: Relativistic MHD of QGP in strong magnetic fields
summary: Off-central heavy-ion collisions create fields eB ~ m_pi^2 (about 1e18 G); relativistic MHD codes developed for astrophysical plasmas model how the conducting QGP responds, affecting directed flow and charge-dependent observables.
breaks: The QGP's electrical conductivity is low (sigma ~ 0.01 fm^-1), so the magnetic Reynolds number is small and ideal-MHD flux freezing does not apply.
sources: Inghirami et al. (2016). "Numerical magneto-hydrodynamics for relativistic nuclear collisions". *Eur. Phys. J. C* 76, 659. [arXiv:1609.03042](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.03042)

name: BUU/Vlasov transport for heavy-ion reactions
summary: Intermediate-energy heavy-ion collisions are simulated with Boltzmann-Uehling-Uhlenbeck transport: a Vlasov equation in the nuclear mean field plus a Pauli-blocked collision term; giant resonances appear as nuclear zero sound with Landau damping.
breaks: Nuclear transport uses a self-consistent short-range mean field rather than long-range Coulomb fields, and Pauli blocking with quantum fluctuations makes it semiclassical at best.
sources: Buss et al. (2012). "Transport-theoretical Description of Nuclear Reactions". *Phys. Rep.* 512, 1. [arXiv:1106.1344](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.1344)

name: Tritium breeding and neutron transport in blankets
summary: A D-T power plant must breed its tritium from lithium blankets: 6Li(n,t)alpha and 7Li(n,n't)alpha cross sections, neutron multiplication by Be or Pb (n,2n) and transport set the tritium breeding ratio, which must exceed 1.
breaks: Blanket designs depend on evaluated cross sections with nontrivial uncertainties for 14 MeV neutrons and on engineering coverage losses.

name: Fusion neutron spectroscopy as plasma diagnostic
summary: Neutron time-of-flight and activation detectors measure ICF and tokamak yields; the Doppler width of the 14.1 MeV neutron line gives the ion temperature and down-scattered neutrons give the fuel areal density.
breaks: Bulk flow and anisotropic motion broaden the line too, so apparent ion temperatures can exceed thermal ones.
sources: Brysk (1973). "Fusion neutron energies and spectra". *Plasma Phys.* 15, 611. [doi:10.1088/0032-1028/15/7/001](https://doi.org/10.1088/0032-1028/15/7/001)

name: Nuclear reaction rates measured in laser-driven plasmas
summary: Inertial-fusion implosions reach stellar-core temperatures and densities, letting reactions such as T+T and 3He+3He be measured in a thermal plasma environment with plasma screening, complementing accelerator beam-target data.
map: Y=\int n_1n_2\langle\sigma v\rangle(T_i)\,dV\,dt;\ \text{infer }S(E_0)\text{ at Gamow peak}
breaks: Implosion temperatures and densities vary in space and time, so extracting a reactivity requires hydrodynamic modelling.
sources: Casey et al. (2017). "Thermonuclear reactions probed at stellar-core conditions with laser-based inertial-confinement fusion". *Nature Phys.* 13, 1227. [doi:10.1038/nphys4220](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys4220)

name: Laser-plasma ion and neutron sources for nuclear physics
summary: Intense laser-plasma interactions accelerate MeV ions and produce bremsstrahlung and neutron bursts that drive nuclear reactions, isotope production and photonuclear experiments with ultrashort, ultradense pulses.
map: E_{\max}^{\rm TNSA}\sim2T_{\rm hot}\ln^2(\cdots),\ T_{\rm hot}\approx m_ec^2(\sqrt{1+a_0^2/2}-1)
breaks: Laser-driven beams have broad spectra and low repetition rates compared with accelerators.

name: Albedo neutron decay feeds the inner radiation belt
summary: Cosmic rays striking the atmosphere make albedo neutrons, and those that beta-decay inside the magnetosphere leave trapped protons (CRAND), the main source of high-energy protons in Earth's inner radiation belt; the free-neutron lifetime sets the injection rate.
breaks: Radial diffusion and losses, not the source term alone, set belt intensities.
sources: Singer (1958). "Trapped Albedo Theory of the Radiation Belt". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 1, 181. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.1.181](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.1.181)

name: Radiation dosimetry in space weather
summary: Solar energetic particle events and trapped radiation are quantified with nuclear dosimetry quantities (absorbed dose, quality factors, LET spectra) to protect astronauts and electronics; detectors aboard spacecraft are nuclear-physics instruments.
breaks: Space fields are mixed and highly variable, and heavy ions dominate biological dose despite small fluences.

name: Nuclear gamma-ray lines from flare-accelerated ions
summary: Reconnection-accelerated protons and alphas in solar flares hit the solar atmosphere and excite nuclear lines (4.44 MeV 12C, 6.13 MeV 16O) and the 2.223 MeV neutron-capture line, which measure the ion spectrum and composition of reconnection acceleration.
map: p+{}^{12}\mathrm C\to p'+{}^{12}\mathrm C^*(4.44);\ n+p\to d+\gamma(2.223\ \text{MeV})
breaks: Line yields fold together acceleration, transport and target geometry, so the inferred ion spectrum is model-dependent.

name: ECR plasma ion sources for radioactive beams
summary: Electron-cyclotron-resonance plasma ion sources and charge breeders produce the highly charged ions that drive and reaccelerate radioactive-beam facilities (FRIB, ISOLDE), applying magnetized discharge plasma physics to exotic-nucleus production.
breaks: ECR sources are engineered for high charge states, a regime far from processing plasmas.

name: Ionization-dependent beta decay in stellar plasmas
summary: In hot plasmas nuclei are highly ionized, which opens bound-state beta decay and closes electron capture from atomic orbitals; fully ionized 187Re decays about 1e9 times faster, changing the Re-Os cosmochronometer and s-process branchings.
breaks: Rates depend on plasma ionization balance and continuum electron density, so they need plasma models in addition to nuclear matrix elements.
sources: Langanke & Martínez-Pinedo (2003). "Nuclear weak-interaction processes in stars". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 75, 819. [arXiv:nucl-th/0203071](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0203071)

name: Applied nuclear physics underpins medical physics
summary: Radiotherapy, nuclear medicine and radiation protection rest on nuclear data, radiation-matter interactions and detector physics developed in applied nuclear physics.

name: Evaluated nuclear data for medical applications
summary: Medical isotope choice, activity calculations and dose models need evaluated half-lives, decay schemes, emission spectra and production cross sections from nuclear data libraries.
sources: Brown et al. (2018). "ENDF/B-VIII.0: The 8th Major Release of the Nuclear Reaction Data Library with CIELO-project Cross Sections, New Standards and Thermal Scattering Data". *Nucl. Data Sheets* 148, 1. [doi:10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nds.2018.02.001)

name: Radiation detection and dosimetry in the clinic
summary: Clinical dosimetry (ionization chambers, calibration protocols, Gy and Sv) and imaging detectors are nuclear radiation-detection physics applied to patients.

name: Isotope production for nuclear medicine and PET
summary: PET and SPECT depend on producing short-lived isotopes (18F, 11C, 68Ga, 99mTc) and theranostic pairs (177Lu, 225Ac) through reactions chosen by cross section, yield, purity and half-life.

name: Bragg peak and dosimetry in radiation therapy
summary: Charged-particle stopping (Bethe formula, Bragg peak) and photon interaction physics determine depth-dose curves; dosimetry calibration underlies treatment delivery.
sources: Wilson (1946). "Radiological Use of Fast Protons". *Radiology* 47, 487. [doi:10.1148/47.5.487](https://doi.org/10.1148/47.5.487)

name: Coupled cluster: from nuclei to chemistry and back
summary: Coupled-cluster theory was invented for nuclear matter (Coester, Kümmel), developed into the gold standard of quantum chemistry (Cizek, CCSD(T)), and returned to nuclear physics for medium-mass nuclei with chiral forces.
breaks: Nuclear CC must handle three-nucleon forces and self-bound centre-of-mass motion, while chemistry has a fixed nuclear frame and Coulomb-only interactions.
sources: Coester (1958). "Bound states of a many-particle system". *Nucl. Phys.* 7, 421. [doi:10.1016/0029-5582(58)90280-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(58)90280-3)

Čížek (1966). "On the Correlation Problem in Atomic and Molecular Systems. Calculation of Wavefunction Components in Ursell-Type Expansion Using Quantum-Field Theoretical Methods". *J. Chem. Phys.* 45, 4256. [doi:10.1063/1.1727484](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1727484)
Hagen et al. (2014). "Coupled-cluster computations of atomic nuclei". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 77, 096302. [arXiv:1312.7872](https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.7872)

name: PET and SPECT detectors are nuclear gamma detectors
summary: Gamma cameras and PET scanners use scintillators (LSO/LYSO, NaI), photomultipliers or SiPMs and coincidence timing from nuclear spectroscopy; time-of-flight PET localizes annihilation along the line of response.
sources: Jan et al. (2004). "GATE: a simulation toolkit for PET and SPECT". *Phys. Med. Biol.* 49, 4543. [arXiv:physics/0408109](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0408109)

name: Positron emission physics sets PET resolution
summary: PET imaging is beta-plus decay followed by positron thermalization and annihilation; the beta endpoint energy sets the positron range (18F 0.6 mm vs 82Rb ~6 mm) and residual momentum gives annihilation non-collinearity, the two physical limits on PET resolution.
breaks: The positron range depends on tissue density and on the full beta spectrum, not only the endpoint.
sources: Jan et al. (2004). "GATE: a simulation toolkit for PET and SPECT". *Phys. Med. Biol.* 49, 4543. [arXiv:physics/0408109](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0408109)

name: Decay chains in generators and alpha theranostics
summary: Radionuclide generators (99Mo/99mTc, 68Ge/68Ga) work by transient or secular equilibrium in Bateman decay chains, and targeted alpha therapy with 225Ac must track recoiling daughters along the decay chain.
breaks: Daughter recoil energies (~100 keV) break chemical bonds, so the chain can leave the targeting molecule, which simple Bateman bookkeeping ignores.

name: Nuclear interactions in proton and ion therapy
summary: Therapeutic proton and carbon beams undergo nuclear reactions that fragment the beam, deposit dose beyond the Bragg peak and produce prompt gammas and positron emitters (11C, 15O) used for in-vivo range verification.
breaks: Nuclear cross sections for therapy-relevant fragments are known only to 10-20 percent, limiting range-verification accuracy.
sources: Wilson (1946). "Radiological Use of Fast Protons". *Radiology* 47, 487. [doi:10.1148/47.5.487](https://doi.org/10.1148/47.5.487)
Min et al. (2006). "Prompt gamma measurements for locating the dose falloff region in the proton therapy". *Appl. Phys. Lett.* 89, 183517. [doi:10.1063/1.2378561](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2378561)

name: Boron neutron capture therapy
summary: BNCT delivers a thermal-neutron field to tumours loaded with 10B; the 10B(n,alpha)7Li reaction deposits ~2.3 MeV within one cell diameter, so the nuclear cross section and short ion ranges give cellular-level targeting.
breaks: Clinical dose depends on boron biodistribution and accelerator-based epithermal neutron sources rather than on nuclear data alone.

name: Nuclear magnetic moments behind MRI
summary: MRI images the precession of nuclear spins; the Larmor frequencies of 1H, 13C, 19F, 23Na and 31P come from nuclear magnetic moments (Schmidt-line shell-model values plus core polarization), first measured by Rabi's resonance method.
breaks: MRI contrast comes from relaxation and chemistry of the environment (T1, T2), not from nuclear structure.
sources: Rabi et al. (1938). "A New Method of Measuring Nuclear Magnetic Moment". *Phys. Rev.* 53, 318. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.53.318](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.53.318)
Lauterbur (1973). "Image Formation by Induced Local Interactions: Examples Employing Nuclear Magnetic Resonance". *Nature* 242, 190. [doi:10.1038/242190a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/242190a0)

name: Medical cyclotrons and isotope production
summary: Lawrence's cyclotron was built for nuclear reactions and today's compact medical cyclotrons and linacs make PET and SPECT isotopes; yields follow from excitation functions, beam current and target stopping power.
breaks: Target cooling and chemistry, not beam physics, often limit practical yields.
